about: Lint's own writing fixtures: English proofreading and tone rewrites (also the English inside mixed Chinese-English text, whose Chinese is left alone), English-to-Traditional-Chinese translation for reference, and the native-speaker tone (Chinese, another language, mixed or broken English in, a native speaker's English out) in its styles (standard, casual, formal, Gen Z and concise); and English that is correct but not what a native speaker would say, whose fix has to keep the writer's voice (keepsVoice), including sentences built wrong (a subject said twice, clauses out of order) around file and product names in another script. Every sentence was written for this repository; nothing is taken from a benchmark corpus. They exist to compare engines on Lint's actual workload, not to score a model in general.

cases.input: 這個流程真的很爛，每次都要重填一樣的資料，到底是誰設計的？
cases.note: Gen Z: slang is welcome here, the frustration keeps its strength; no emoji, nothing added about who designed it.

cases.input: Hello, I want to ask you about the invoice what I send last week, you have receive it or not?
mustFix: you have receive it or not
cases.note: Gen Z: a quick, casual check on last week's invoice; not a pile of slang.

cases.input: Kindly revert back to me at the earliest.
cases.note: A polite written request: "get back to me as soon as you can". Stays a request, adds no greeting or sign-off.

cases.input: lol sorry, I forgot to open the VPN before the call, that's why I dropped.
cases.note: "turn on / connect to the VPN". Stays a casual chat message: lol, contractions, no apology formula.

cases.input: This tool is really not convenient! Every time I must fill the same form again. Who designed this?
cases.note: An annoyed complaint: "such a pain", "I have to fill out". Keeps the exclamation, the rhetorical question and the bluntness; not softened into a polite suggestion.

cases.input: I think maybe we can consider to postpone the launch one week, because the testing is not enough.
cases.note: A hedged suggestion: "push the launch back a week", "we haven't tested enough". Keeps a hedge (I think / maybe); does not become a firm recommendation.

cases.input: May I know when you will be free to have a call with us?
cases.note: A polite question to a client: "When would you be available for a call?". Stays a polite question, adds no greeting or sign-off.

cases.input: Our team will do a sharing session about the new API on Friday, everyone is welcome to join!
cases.note: "host a session / give a talk". Keeps the upbeat exclamation and the open invitation.

cases.input: Thanks for your help today, you really saved my life 🙏 I owe you one meal.
cases.note: "I owe you lunch / a meal". Keeps the emoji and the warm, casual thanks.

cases.input: The deployment has been finished and the service is running normally now.
cases.note: "The deployment is done and the service is back to normal". A neutral status line, no added detail.

cases.input: Sorry for letting you wait so long. The report is still in progress and I will send it to you before 5 pm.
cases.note: "Sorry to keep you waiting". The writer spells out "I will": no contractions added, no extra apology.

cases.input: Please do the needful and update the ticket. Thanks in advance.
cases.note: Drop "do the needful" ("Please update the ticket"). Stays a short request with the writer's own thanks, not a question.

cases.input: Sorry, this request we cannot accept, because it is out of our scope.
cases.note: A clear refusal: "we cannot take this on; it is outside our scope". Stays a refusal: no hedge (might, perhaps), no offer the writer did not make, no contractions added.

cases.input: hey, do you have time now? I wanna discuss with you about the release plan
cases.note: "talk to you about / go over the release plan". Stays a quick casual ping: hey, wanna, lowercase, the question.

cases.input: Can you send me the slides? I want to take a reference.
cases.note: "use them as a reference". Stays a direct, friendly question; "I'd like to" would be more formal than the writer.

cases.input: ugh, the build broke again 😩 can someone take a look?
cases.note: Already natural chat: leave it, lowercase and emoji included.

cases.input: We regret to inform you that the event has been cancelled due to the weather.
cases.note: Already natural formal notice (British spelling): leave it.

cases.input: Honestly, I'm not sure this is worth the effort. Can we talk it through tomorrow?
cases.note: Already natural and hedged: leave it.

cases.input: Quick question: is the staging server down, or is it just me?
cases.note: Already natural: leave it.

cases.input: I would like to inform you that the meeting has been rescheduled to Thursday at 3 pm.
mustFix: I would like to inform you
cases.note: Relaxed: "Heads up, the meeting's moved to Thursday at 3 pm." Same facts, no formula.

cases.input: Please be advised that the server will be unavailable tonight due to scheduled maintenance.
cases.note: Relaxed: the server's down tonight for maintenance. Keeps tonight and the reason.

cases.input: Thank you very much for your assistance. I sincerely appreciate your help with the report.
cases.note: Relaxed thanks for the help with the report; one warm sentence is enough.

cases.input: Could you kindly confirm whether you will be attending the dinner on Friday?
cases.note: Relaxed: are you coming to dinner on Friday? Stays a question.

cases.input: 不好意思打擾一下，想跟您確認一下，就是我們下週三下午兩點的那個會議，請問是不是還是照原本的時間進行呢？
cases.note: Concise English: is next Wednesday's 2 pm meeting still on? Keeps the day and time, drops the throat-clearing.

cases.input: 關於這個問題，我覺得其實我們可以先不要急著做決定，先觀察個一兩週，看看使用者的反應再說，這樣比較保險。
cases.note: Concise English: hold off on deciding; watch user feedback for a week or two first. Keeps the hedge and the time span.

cases.input: 我想跟大家說一下，因為伺服器明天早上九點到十點要做維護，所以那段時間系統會沒辦法使用，請大家提前做好準備，謝謝。
cases.note: Concise English: the system is down tomorrow 9-10 am for server maintenance; plan ahead. Keeps both times and the request.

cases.input: 這份報告我已經從頭到尾仔細看過一遍了，基本上沒有什麼太大的問題，只有第三頁的數字好像需要再確認一下。
cases.note: Concise English: I've read the report; it looks fine, but the numbers on page 3 need checking. Keeps page 3.

cases.input: AI said the request item in the quotation file Daehan-20260115_SSD 견적(테스트코리아).xls, the request item "삼성 SSD 1TB 중고" is second-hand, is it?
cases.note: The subject is said twice: one sentence, e.g. AI said the request item "…" in the quotation file … is second-hand, is that right? The Korean file and product names stay exactly as written, and it stays a question.

cases.input: The server we deployed it yesterday, the server is keep restarting every ten minutes, we still not find the reason.
cases.note: Three clauses run together around a repeated subject: "The server we deployed yesterday keeps restarting every ten minutes, and we still haven't found the reason." Every fact kept.

cases.input: For the budget of next quarter, because the vendor price is not yet come, so we cannot yet finalize it.
cases.note: Topic first, then because … so: "We cannot finalize next quarter's budget yet because the vendor's pricing has not come in." Stays a plain statement with full forms.

cases.input: The meeting room on the fifth floor, the meeting room is already booked by another team until 3 pm, is it?
cases.note: The subject is said twice: "The meeting room on the fifth floor is already booked by another team until 3 pm, isn't it?" Stays a question; 3 pm kept.

cases.input: About the file レポート_0314.xlsx, in the file the delivery date is written wrong, should be March 14 not March 4.
mustFix: in the file the delivery date is written wrong
cases.note: Topic-comment order: "The delivery date in レポート_0314.xlsx is wrong; it should be March 14, not March 4." The Japanese file name and both dates stay.

cases.input: The vendor confirmed that the item "삼성 SSD 1TB" in 견적서_0115.xlsx is new, so we can go ahead with the order.
cases.note: Already a well-built sentence, Korean names and all: leave it.
